title: Depth moment and failure probabilities
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $\delta$ be any real number. For each subset $J$ of coordinates and each assignment $z$ of signs outside $J$, let $d(J,z)$ be the minimum depth of a binary decision tree computing the function obtained by fixing those outside coordinates; define $q_k$ to be the random-restriction average of the indicator of $k\le d(J,z)$, using weight $\delta^{|J|}(1-\delta)^{n-|J|}$ for $J$ and a uniform average over $z$. Then the random-restriction average of $2^{d(J,z)}$ is $1+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}2^j q_{j+1}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is sign-valued on the sign cube
